clue.text: First man with a set of religious texts is resolute

blocks.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a collection of sacred books

explanation.surface: A man holding his scriptures stands firm in his convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant refuses to be moved, which is what being firmly determined means.

clue.text: Passion of artist turning grim

indicators.note: turning round makes the short word for artist face the other way

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
dour means stern and gloomy

explanation.surface: A painter's enthusiasm curdles into a bleak mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense feeling or zeal, a close synonym for strong enthusiasm or love.

clue.text: No limits to damp and haze on river

indicators.note: losing its limits means a word is stripped of its first and last letters, leaving the inside

blocks.note: the inside of damp
the inside of haze
taken as written

explanation.surface: Endless humidity and mist hang over a waterway, like a jungle scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great South American river flowing through the rainforest of Brazil.

clue.text: Eloquent liar ate cut in pieces

indicators.note: broken into pieces, the words are scattered and can be reassembled in a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking fibber eats a portion that has been chopped up.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulate person expresses ideas fluently and clearly, which is what eloquence means.

clue.text: Heads of the wealthy elite rabidly praise buffoon

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Rich bigwigs fanatically applaud a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Twerp is an informal insult for a silly, foolish person, much like a clown or idiot.

clue.text: Rude old boy on site

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a scene is the place where something happens

explanation.surface: A former pupil behaves crudely at some location.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene describes language or behaviour that is offensively indecent or vulgar.

clue.text: Newspaper article about journalists being tyrannised

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

blocks.note: an op-ed is an opinion article opposite the editorial page
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A column about reporters being bullied by a regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The op-ed is named for sitting opposite the editorial page; here the hyphenated word is split open to take the journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: To be oppressed is to be kept down by harsh, unjust authority, as by a tyrant.

clue.text: Plunder fire axe

blocks.note: first meaning: to loot a captured town
second meaning: to dismiss from a job
third meaning: to cut or get rid of, likewise dismissing

explanation.surface: Raiders loot a fire-fighting hatchet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire axe' reads as one object, but it is two separate meanings of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means looting a captured city and also dismissing someone from employment, which fire and axe both express.

clue.text: Issued title returned by upset duke

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a title is a name
as in 'what's eating him?': ate means bothered or upset
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A disgruntled duke hands a title back.
explanation.walkthrough: EMAN + ATE + D. 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym: something that eats at you upsets you.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanated means flowed out or came forth from a source, as an issued statement does.

clue.text: Engineer set a time to assess

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters are built into another arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer books a slot to carry out an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge or calculate roughly, the sense of appraise or evaluate.

clue.text: Doctor behind plan

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
aft is the nautical word for at the back

explanation.surface: A physician is the one responsible for a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word but supplies its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary sketch or outline version of a scheme or document.

clue.text: Former pet can't mix with child

indicators.note: to mix things is to jumble them up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: ex means former
the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: An old pet that won't get along with a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With child' reads as company for the pet; it is the old phrase for pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant mother is pregnant, and 'with child' is the old-fashioned idiom for pregnancy.

clue.text: Coup, induced almost entirely in error, is doing nothing

indicators.note: almost entirely means all but a tiny bit, so the last letter is dropped
in error means wrongly arranged, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
induced loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A mistakenly provoked revolt turns out to achieve nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unoccupied describes someone idle, without work or activity to keep them busy.

clue.text: Comfort found in herbal medicine

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Relief can be had from plant-based remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal: a balm is itself a soothing herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm is something soothing, figuratively anything that brings solace or relief.

clue.text: Information found in most unusual ecosystem

indicators.note: one thing found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: rarest is the superlative of rare, unusual
info is short for information

explanation.surface: Data is discovered in an exceptionally strange natural habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' could signal a hidden word, but no run of letters here spells the answer; it puts one synonym inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainforest is a dense tropical woodland, a distinct biological community and habitat.

clue.text: Modest talent written about in books

indicators.note: written about suggests letters scribbled every which way, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer of small gifts gets reviewed in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' is plural because the answer is a whole collection of biblical books.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament is the first part of the Christian Bible, made up of many separate books.

clue.text: Behaviour management

blocks.note: first meaning: the way one acts towards someone
second meaning: the handling of a patient or condition

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like the title of a course; they are separate meanings of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both how you behave towards someone and the medical care or handling of an illness.

clue.text: Mimes hid out and danced

indicators.note: out here means disordered or wrong, so the letters are set in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Street performers stayed concealed and then jigged about.
explanation.definitionFit: To shimmy is to dance by shaking the shoulders and hips, so it is a kind of dancing.

clue.text: Singer in argument after footballers left

indicators.note: after says the argument piece comes second, following the footballers and left

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association, governing English football
L is the abbreviation for left
a set-to is a fight or quarrel

explanation.surface: A vocalist gets into a row once the team has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed in the surface; here it is just its one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is a male voice singing above its natural range, here standing for the performer using it.

clue.text: Agonising trial involving Vogue

indicators.note: to involve is to enclose or include, so the first piece goes round the second

blocks.note: a hearing is a court trial
a vogue is a fashion or trend

explanation.surface: A painful court case concerning a fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Vogue, capitalised, looks like the fashion magazine, but it is just the common noun for a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartrending means causing deep grief or anguish, the sense of something excruciating.

clue.text: Lustre surrounding top of Russian place of worship

indicators.note: surrounding means going round another piece
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: lustre is shine or gloss
the first letter of Russian

explanation.surface: The gleam around an Orthodox church's dome.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a holy site or building dedicated to a saint or deity, visited for prayer.

clue.text: Weep about European record being unsettling

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the others

blocks.note: to weep is to cry
E is the abbreviation for European
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Crying over a European disc that is disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: An EP, extended play, is a record longer than a single but shorter than an album.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy means causing an uneasy feeling of fear or disquiet, the sense of disturbing.

clue.text: Blur lost on radio

indicators.note: on radio a word is heard rather than seen, so its sound matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: lost, as in failed to catch, is missed

explanation.surface: A broadcast signal fades into indistinctness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a haze of fine droplets, and figuratively anything that makes vision indistinct or hazy.

clue.text: Sulks about test woman gives relative

indicators.note: turned about means faced the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, so sulks are pets
the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness check for cars
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone moping over an exam she sat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' looks like the exam; in crosswords it is often the MOT, Britain's annual vehicle safety inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepmother is a father's wife who is not your birth mother, a family member by marriage.

clue.text: Excuse leader of the fold

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: a plea is a pretext or excuse
the first letter of the

explanation.surface: A pretext offered by the head of a flock of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' suggests a sheep pen; it is a crease in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed or sewn into cloth, such as in a skirt.

clue.text: Crow costume turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: garb is clothing or dress

explanation.surface: A blackbird outfit appears at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird, but it is the verb for boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, exactly the sense of showing off about one's achievements.

clue.text: Barge in Bury free to move around

indicators.note: moving letters around shifts them into another order

blocks.note: to inter is to bury a body
the letters of free, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone intrudes on Bury, the Lancashire town, which wants to be at liberty to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' wants to be the town near Manchester, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in is to intrude where one is not wanted, the same as meddling or interfering.

clue.text: European diet is best

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
lite is the label for diet, low-calorie products

explanation.surface: A slimming regime from the continent is the top option.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the choicest or finest members of a group, the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Daughter having bad time in dry spell

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
rough means unpleasant or bad
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A girl going through a hard patch during a period without rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long period with little or no rainfall, so an extended arid stretch.

clue.text: Unsteady river animal in banks of Tay

indicators.note: a river's banks are its edges, so only the outside letters of the word are kept
in means placed inside the other letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of Tay
an otter is an aquatic mammal living by rivers

explanation.surface: A wobbly otter perched on the banks of a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: OTTER goes between T and Y. The Tay is Scotland's longest river, and 'banks' fits it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means shaky and liable to fall, like someone walking without balance.
